candidate.scope: The single, unbranched Illumina Drop-Seq schematic, interpreted at its depicted level using the original Macosko et al. (2015) implementation: droplet-isolated cells, barcoded oligo(dT) capture beads, pooling before bulk cDNA synthesis/amplification, and sequencing of a cDNA-derived 3′-end expression library. The left cell-to-poly(A)-RNA icon explains the target rather than adding a separate preparation operation; the bead legend explains an input component. Catalogue-listed similar methods and papers about other assays do not create additional targets.

operations.label: cDNA synthesis and amplification
operations.description: In bulk, copy captured mRNAs from bead-attached primers into barcode-bearing cDNA and amplify the cDNA. The broad depicted block is connected to sequencing through the primary paper’s cDNA-derived 3′-end DNA library interface. The catalogue statement that a PCR primer sequence replaces the universal sequence is not adopted: the primary source describes the original universal region as a downstream PCR/sequencing priming site and template switching as introducing an additional PCR handle downstream of synthesized cDNA.
operations.mechanism: Bead-primer reverse transcription with template switching to add a downstream PCR handle, followed by PCR amplification. The primary implementation prepares the sequencing library from amplified cDNA using Nextera XT with primers selecting transcript 3′ ends; this is clarification within the broad block, not an additional depicted operation.
operations.information_effect: Covalently links bead cell barcode and primer UMI to transcript-derived DNA; amplification creates copies that retain those identifiers.
